root.name: Amar Gambit
root.moves: 1. Nh3 d5 2. g3 e5 3. f4 Bxh3 4. Bxh3 exf4

overview: In the Amar Paris Gambit White has traded off the light bishops and Black has taken on f4. White can recapture with gxf4 for an open g-file or play Nf3 and d4 for the centre, accepting that Black is a pawn up with the better structure.

white_ideas.idea: Regain f4 or play d4 and Nc3 with open lines for the Bh3
Use the open g-file after gxf4 against the king

black_ideas.idea: Hold the extra pawn with ...Nf6 and ...c6

typical_structures.structure: White has lost the f-pawn exchange; Black has an extra f4 pawn

character.notes: Very unbalanced: White has given a pawn for vague play.

gambit.notes: White is a pawn down after ...exf4 and can only regain it with gxf4 or d4 tricks.

soundness.notes: Not objectively sound; Black can keep the pawn.

structure.notes: Open e- and f-files after the exchanges.

level.notes: Few plans to learn; unsound so not a first choice.

character.reason: White sacrifices a pawn for open lines.

gambit.reason: White is a pawn down with no forced return.

structure.reason: Files e and f are open.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White tries to use development against the king.
